newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures correct to end firmer but trend down.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures correct to end firmer but trend down.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed firmer in a technical correction, but the overall trend remains lower, market analysts said.

"This is just a technical bounce from an oversold condition," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said. "The market made new contract lows yesterday and it may have inspired bottom-picking but the situation is still negative."

The spot July contract settled 1.65 cents higher at 74.30 cents per lb, traded 75.40 to 72.50 cents. The most-active September contract ended up 1.70 cents at 77.20 cents, while the rest of the board finished 1.50 to 2.40 higher.
Floor sources said early fund selling failed to garner momentum, prompting the locals and trade to cover short positions.
Today's gains are likely to be shortlived, however, as the fundamental picture is expected to put constant pressure on the market.

Activity over the next week will focus on the liquidation of July ahead of first notice day on July 1. Open interest in the spot contract remains high at 12,416 lots, down 474 lots as of early Monday.
An estimated 7,200 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 9,930 lots.
